subject: Request: high-availability commitment for OrbitX — product questions & proposal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kiran Patel <kiran@orbitx.ai>
Cc: Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@orbitx.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitX HA commitment conversation

Hi Kiran — thanks for the detailed note and for sharing the context on expected traffic. We’re keen to support OrbitX as a strategic partner. A couple of quick clarifying questions so we scope the commitment correctly:

- Is the 800 qps target concurrent sustained or burstable (90th pct of business hours)?
- Are the p99 targets for single-token generation or end-to-end latency (API request -> final token)?
- Any hard constraints on data residency/region requirements for the serving cluster?

High level — we do offer tailored availability/latency commitments for key accounts, but they typically require a Dedicated capacity reservation + operational runbook (canary, failover, fallback model variants). If OrbitX is open to a one-month pilot on a reserved pool we can instrument and validate an SLO before committing formally.

I’m looping in product and infra to quickly validate feasibility and a rough cost delta. Can you send the technical requirements (payload size, typical sequence lengths, expected burst profile) so we can model it?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: none
From: Kiran Patel <kiran@orbitx.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitX HA commitment conversation

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick response. Answers below and I attached a short tech spec.

- 800 qps is our steady-state minimum during peak hours; bursts up to ~1.4k qps for <10 minute windows.
- p99 target is end-to-end API latency (we measure 95th percentile for tokens internally; we'd like a conservative p99 for SLA). Target: p99 < 220ms, p95 < 120ms.
- Data must remain in us-west region. We can accept dedicated tenancy but prefer not to self-host initially.

Attached: orbitx_tech_requirements.xlsx (includes average sequence length = 120 tokens, payload size ~18KB compressed).

We’d like a commitment by next week if possible — we’re lining up procurement and legal.

Cheers,
Kiran Patel
Head of Platform | OrbitX
Attachment: orbitx_tech_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T19:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: OrbitX HA commitment — product + legal inputs

Forwarding OrbitX requirements. Key asks from the customer: sustain 800 qps, burst to 1.4k qps, p99 < 220ms end-to-end, us-west only. They’re asking for a formal commitment within ~1 week to feed procurement.

Product/Infra asks (please respond inline):
- Feasibility: can we meet p99 < 220ms under sustained 800 qps with Dedicated capacity in us-west given their seq length (120 tokens) and payload sizes?
- Suggested guarding rails: what dedicated pool size (GPU count/types), recommended autoscaling headroom, and whether prefix/KV caching or model quantization is required to hit targets without overprovisioning.
- Operational: what runbook items do we require in the contract (canary plan, rollback trigger, cold-start behaviors)?
- Cost delta: quick ballpark monthly delta vs standard hosted usage (we need a number to present to procurement).

Jonas — please flag any legal redlines for committing to p99 numbers (e.g., force majeure language, SLO credits formula) so we can include a line in the proposal.

I’ll coordinate a 30-min sync if needed, but would prefer short answers we can put into a one-page commitment.

Thanks — Marissa
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: OrbitX HA commitment — product + legal inputs

Short answers and recommendations below. I ran a quick model based on the attached spec. Attached is a simple cost delta CSV.

Feasibility: Yes — with Dedicated capacity in us-west and a tailored configuration we can meet p99 < 220ms for 800 sustained qps given 120-token seqs. Key assumptions: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (or 12x smaller T4-equivalents with heavier batching), 10% reserved headroom, and continuous prefix/KV caching for common prefixes.

Recommended configuration (minimal viable commit):
- Dedicated pool: 8 A100-eq GPUs pinned to OrbitX (us-west).
- Autoscale policy: buffer to allow 1.75x burst for short windows (scale guided by 5-min rolling p95).
- Model variant: use 8-bit quantized variant for cost/perf tradeoff; we keep a higher-precision fallback (no SLA on fallback).
- Caching: mandatory prefix/KV caching for their top 200 prompt templates.

Operational runbook items (to include in contract):
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor p95/p99 and tail latencies.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p99 > 250ms for 15 minutes or error rate increase > 0.5% absolute.
- Failover: automatic regional fallback disabled (per data residency) — instead we provide documented manual failover and extended support hours.

Cost delta: ~USD 18,000/month on top of standard hosted usage for reserved capacity + 10% ops premium (see attached orb_req_cost_model.csv). This assumes Redwood absorbs one month of trial cost and procurement signs up for 3+ month term.

Caveats: we need legal to review the SLO credit formula and lock the wording around out-of-scope events. Also product needs time (~3 weeks) to pin the dedicated pool and run the pilot instrumentation.

Attachment: orb_req_cost_model.csv (csv)

- Grace
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kiran Patel <kiran@orbitx.ai>, Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@orbitx.ai>, OrbitX Procurement <procurement@orbitx.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: OrbitX proposed resiliency commitment (pilot + SLO draft)

Kiran / Alex — thank you for the quick turnaround. Per internal review we can offer the following path forward:

Proposed pilot (1 month):
- Dedicated us-west pool: 8 A100-eq GPUs reserved for OrbitX.
- Objective: validate p99 < 220ms at sustained 800 qps and short bursts to 1.4k qps.
- Instrumentation: full tracing and token-level latency breakdowns shared weekly.
- Trial credit: Redwood will cover the pilot cost for the first 30 days; subsequent months billed under a reserved capacity contract.

SLO (post-pilot, suggested contract language):
- Commitment: Monthly availability 99.95% for API access in us-west; p99 latency target of 220ms for end-to-end requests as measured by Redwood’s telemetry from the dedicated pool.
- Remedies: SLO credits calculated as % of monthly reserved fee if Redwood misses availability > 0.05% or p99 misses for more than two calendar days in a 30-day window.
- Out-of-scope: force majeure, OrbitX-configured third-party integrations, data residency enforced manual failovers.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you accept the pilot plan and we’ll draft a one-page amendment and a DocuSign to get procurement moving.
2) If accepted, product will schedule a 2-hour onboarding call with your platform team next week to pin pooling and caching settings.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/secure/ORB-4271-proposal

If that looks good I’ll route the one-pager to procurement and Jonas will add the legal SLO language.

Best,
Marissa
Attachment: proposal_orbitx_docusign.pdf (pdf)
